# Fortran

<!-- Generated by bazel run //tools/docs/languages:languages_bin -- --write from fortran/lang.json and fortran/defs.bzl. Do not edit. -->

This page helps you build, test and check Fortran code with rules_dx.

## Quick start

`MODULE.bazel` sits at the root of your repository and lists the Bazel modules, meaning external dependencies, that your project uses. Add `rules_dx` to it:

```python
bazel_dep(name = "rules_dx", version = "<release>")
```

Then let dx set up the rest, as in the [Quickstart](../../README.md#quickstart):

```sh
bazel run @rules_dx//dx/launch:dx -- init --apply
```

For a Fortran project, `MODULE.bazel` then looks like this:

```python
module(name = "my_project")

bazel_dep(name = "rules_dx", version = "<release>")
```

A `BUILD.bazel` file declares targets: the libraries, binaries and tests that Bazel builds. This one is a small Fortran package from [`fortran/tests/consumer`](https://github.com/devhusdk/rules_dx/blob/main/fortran/tests/consumer/BUILD.bazel):

```python
load("@rules_dx//fortran:defs.bzl", "fortran_library")

fortran_library(
    name = "fortran",
    srcs = ["greet.f90"],
    visibility = ["//visibility:public"],
)
```

Build and test everything. `//...` means every target in the repository:

```sh
tools/dx test //...
```

## Dependencies

### Modules

A source can `use` modules from the targets in its `deps`. It cannot `use` a
module from another source of the same target. So put each module that other
code uses in its own `fortran_library`, and share it through `deps`:

```python
load("@rules_dx//fortran:defs.bzl", "fortran_library")

fortran_library(
    name = "kinds",
    srcs = ["kinds.f90"],
)

fortran_library(
    name = "units",
    srcs = ["units.f90"],
    deps = [":kinds"],
)
```

Sources in different packages may share a file name, such as `kinds.f90`.
The intrinsic modules (`iso_fortran_env`, `iso_c_binding`, `ieee_*`) need
no dependency.

### Locked packages

List git dependencies in `fpm.toml`. Each one needs a
`https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` URL pinned with `tag` or `rev`. Path
dependencies are skipped.

1. Run `dx update --apply`. It reads the git dependencies of `fpm.toml` and
   of every archive they name, and writes `fpm.lock.json`.
2. Call `fpm.lock(name, lock)` in `MODULE.bazel`. It creates the hub `name`:
   one Bazel repository with a `fortran_library` per locked package.
3. Depend on a package as `@<name>//<package>`.

```python
fpm = use_extension("@rules_dx//fortran:extensions.bzl", "fpm")
fpm.lock(
    name = "fpm",
    lock = "//:fpm.lock.json",
)
use_repo(fpm, "fpm")
```

Each package compiles the Fortran sources under its `src` tree and depends on
the packages its own `fpm.toml` lists. `dx security` and `dx license` list
the locked packages.

## Quality

The default policy selects these tools for the `fortran` family:

| Command | Tool | Files |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dx format` | `ffmt` | `.f90`, `.f95`, `.f03`, `.F90`, `.F95`, `.fpp` |
| `dx lint` | `fortitude`, `typos` | free-form sources: `.f90` and newer |
| `dx typecheck` | `flang` | only when the family sets `typecheck = ["flang"]` |

- ffmt leaves fixed-form `.f` and `.F` files and `.f08` and `.F08` files
  alone, because it would corrupt or reject them.
- fortitude reads free-form source only, so it does not lint `.f` and `.F`
  files.

Fortran targets build with `-fimplicit-none -fimplicit-none-ext -std=f2018
-Werror`, so implicit typing, implicit external procedures, nonstandard
extensions and warnings fail the build. Locked fpm packages build without
them. Set `warnings_as_errors = False` on one target to drop these flags, or
turn them off for the whole build in `.bazelrc`:

```text
common --@rules_dx//config:warnings_as_errors=false
```

## Toolchain

The Fortran runtime, flang-rt, is built from source with the same C++
toolchain as the rest of the build. Binaries and tests link through
`cc_binary` and `cc_test`.

### C interop

A `fortran_library` gives C and C++ rules a `CcInfo`, and it can depend on a
`cc_library`.

- Fortran calling C: declare an `interface` with `bind(c)` and add the
  `cc_library` to `deps`.
- C calling Fortran: write the routine with `bind(c)` and add the
  `fortran_library` to the `deps` of a `cc_binary` or `cc_test`. The runtime
  comes with it.

## Rules

`load` brings rules into a `BUILD.bazel` file. Load the ones you use from `@rules_dx//fortran:defs.bzl`:

```python
load("@rules_dx//fortran:defs.bzl", "fortran_library", "fortran_binary", "fortran_test")
```

### `fortran_library`

```python
fortran_library(name, srcs = None, visibility = None, **kwargs)
```

Thin wrapper over the rules_fortran fortran_library rule.

### `fortran_binary`

```python
fortran_binary(name, *, srcs = None, visibility = None, **kwargs)
```

Compiles Fortran sources with rules_fortran and links them with cc_binary.

### `fortran_test`

```python
fortran_test(name, *, srcs = None, visibility = None, **kwargs)
```

Compiles Fortran sources with rules_fortran and links them with cc_test.

### `fortran_doc_shard`

```python
fortran_doc_shard(name, lib, package = "", **kwargs)
```

Declares the DocIr shard of one Fortran library.

## Tools and package files

dx runs these tools and reads these package files for Fortran:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Tools | `ffmt`, `fortitude` |
| Ecosystems | fpm |
| Manifests | `fpm.toml` |
| Lockfiles | `fpm.lock.json` |

## Platforms

Fortran builds and tests on:

- Linux arm64
- Linux x86_64
- macOS arm64

The [support matrix](../support-matrix.md) lists the platforms. OpenMP,
GPU offload and Wasm are not supported. On Windows, Fortran targets are
incompatible and skipped.

## API docs

`tools/dx docs` builds the API docs with `ford`; see [docs](../cli/commands/docs.md).

To declare a docs target yourself, load the rule behind it:

```python
load("@rules_dx//fortran:defs.bzl", "fortran_doc_shard")
```

`dx docs` documents every `fortran_library` that lists its own sources, with
no setup. FORD parses the public modules, types and procedures on the pinned
Python toolchain. Nothing is compiled and no host tool runs.

To build the shard yourself, declare one:

```python
load("@rules_dx//fortran:defs.bzl", "fortran_doc_shard")

fortran_doc_shard(
    name = "units_docs",
    lib = ":units",
)
```
